text:
lee: Heads up — after yesterday's autoscaler change we saw a big surge of gpu-nodepool scaling but a large percentage of pods stayed Pending. Still investigating but seems tied to a temporary 'quarantine' taint we added during node onboarding.

anika: Ugh, that was the taint we used to stop scheduling while CNI hooks run, right? `node.k8s.redwood/quarantine=true:NoSchedule`?

jordan: Correct. The onboarding job sets that taint until the CNI + device plugin handshake completes. Why would that leave pods Pending after taint removal?

lee: My hunch: we remove the taint *after* the node is visible to the autoscaler as Ready, so autoscaler sees capacity first and schedules, but kube-scheduler still has some affinity/toleration ordering quirks and some daemonset init containers were still pulling images -> pods bounced to Pending while autoscaler kept adding nodes.

maria: Can you paste the `kubectl describe` for a stuck pod?

lee: Sure, short snippet:```
Name:           gpu-worker-0
Node:           <none>
Tolerations:    node.k8s.redwood/quarantine:NoSchedule for 8m
Events:
  Normal  NotTriggerScaleUp  2m    cluster-autoscaler  pod didn't trigger scale-up (it wouldn't fit if a new node is added)
  Warning FailedScheduling   1m    default-scheduler  0/5 nodes are available: 5 node(s) had taint {node.k8s.redwood/quarantine: } that the pod didn't tolerate.
```

kai: That message is consistent with race where taint was reapplied by the onboarding controller after autoscaler started scaling? We had a bug reapplying taints on node status update.

jordan: Also saw IP exhaustion logs on aws-cni around the same time — nodes were Ready but couldn't allocate pod IPs temporarily, causing scheduler to mark as NotReady for pod binding. Combined with re-applied taints, it stalls everything.

anika: So 2 failure modes colliding: (1) taint lifecycle out of sync with autoscaler/scheduler assumptions, (2) CNI IP shortage -> node cannot accept pods even if Ready.

lee: Proposed short-term fixes: turn off reapplication of quarantine taint in onboarding controller (PR ready), and tweak autoscaler to respect node readiness conditions better by adding a 30s buffer before considering a node for scaling decisions.

maria: For IP exhaustion, ops-bot, can you confirm if eni scarcity spiked in wus2 at ~16:15 UTC yesterday?

ops-bot: aws-cni-alert: VPC eni allocation spike detected in region wus2 at 2026-06-12T16:12:43Z. IP utilization peaked at 94% on worker subnet gw-3. See runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/cni-ip-exhaustion

kai: For medium-term: let's change onboarding flow: mark node as `unschedulable` until device plugin Ready, then remove `unschedulable` + taint atomically. That avoids scheduler/CA mismatch. Also enable `--scale-down-unneeded-time` tweak so CA doesn't over-react to transient provisioning.

jordan: Agree. Also consider using a separate nodepool with a softer taint `gpu.warmup=preemptible:PreferNoSchedule` for burst scaling so non-critical workloads don't crowd core GPU pool when spot nodes come up. That reduces cost vs reserving on-demand.

anika: Action items: 1) kai to roll onboarding controller patch to stop reapplying taint (PR #418) — ETA 2h. 2) lee to add 30s CA readiness buffer and test in staging — ETA EOD. 3) maria/infra to evaluate additional ENI capacity in wus2 or move some pods to alternate subnets — sync in 24h. 4) jordan to draft nodepool with `PreferNoSchedule` profile for spot warmup — ETA 48h.

lee: I'm going to drain one affected node and repro flow with verbose logging, will post logs. If anyone sees more Pending pods, ping me in thread. :eyes:
